title: In search of a cut‐off apnea–hypopnea index in type 3 home portable monitors to diagnose and treat obstructive sleep apnea: a mathematical simulation

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Summary</jats:title><jats:p>The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) uses similar apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) cut‐off values to diagnose and define severity of sleep apnea independent of the technique used: in‐hospital polysomnography (PSG) or type 3 portable monitoring (PM). Taking into account that PM theoretically might underestimate the AHI, we explored whether a lower cut‐off would be more appropriate. We performed mathematical re‐calculations on the diagnostic PSG‐AHI (scored using AASM 1999 rules) of 865 consecutive patients with an AHI of ≥20 events/h who started continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP). For a PSG‐AHI of ≥15 events/h re‐scored using AASM 2012 rules (PSG‐AHI<jats:sup>AASM2012</jats:sup>), a PM‐respiratory event index (REI)<jats:sup>AASM2012</jats:sup> cut‐off point of ≥15 events/h resulted in a post‐test probability of 100% of having the disease, but with negative tests in 57.1%. A PM‐REI<jats:sup>AASM2012</jats:sup> cut‐off of 8 events/h, still resulted in a positive post‐test probability of 100% but with negative tests in only 34.3%. Combination of the cut‐off values with clinical estimation of being ‘at high risk’ based on Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and Berlin Questionnaire scores only resulted in a small reduction in the percentage of negative tests (respectively 52.7% and 32.7%). After 6 months, CPAP adherence was not lower using the PM‐REI<jats:sup>AASM 2012</jats:sup> cut‐off ≥8 events/h in comparison to ≥15 events/h (median 5.7 vs. 5.8 h/night, <jats:italic>p</jats:italic> = 0.368) and the reduction in ESS was similar too (median –4 and –5 points, <jats:italic>p</jats:italic> = 0.083). Consequently, using a lower PM‐REI<jats:sup>AASM2012</jats:sup> cut‐off could result in cost savings because of less negative studies and lesser need for a confirmatory PSG or a performance of a CPAP trial.</jats:p>
